docs.text: HardFOC driver Alicat BASIS-2 Driver ¶ A C++17 driver for Alicat BASIS-2 mass flow meters and controllers. It reads flow, temperature and the totalizer, commands setpoints, tares and reconfigures the instruments over Modbus-RTU, on any MCU with a UART and an RS-485 or RS-232 transceiver. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that writes bytes, reads bytes with a timeout and flushes the receive buffer; it does the rest: Modbus-RTU framing, the CRC-16, reply checks, register scaling and error reporting. It is header-only and allocates nothing. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: identify, read, command, tare, set up a bus and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Driver standing for alicat_basis2::Driver<MyUart> and al for alicat_basis2 . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One Driver<UartT> object per instrument. Its calls fall into a few groups: Group Calls Instruments Live data ReadInstantaneous() All Identity ReadIdentity() ; the free function GetDriverVersion() for the driver All Setpoint SetSetpoint() , SetSetpointSource() , SetCommWatchdogMs() , SetMaxSetpointRamp() Controllers Tare Tare() , SetAutotareEnabled() (controllers) All Gas and flow processing SetGas() , SetFlowAveragingMs() , SetReferenceTemperatureC() All Totalizer ResetTotalizer() , SetTotalizerLimitMode() , SetTotalizerBatch() (controllers) All Measurement window ConfigureMeasurementTrigger() (controllers), StartMeasurementSamples() , ReadMeasurement() All Bus configuration SetModbusAddress() , SetAsciiUnitId() , SetBaudRate() , FactoryRestore() , DiscoverPresentAddresses() All Raw access ReadHoldingRegisters() , WriteSingleRegister() , WriteMultipleRegisters() All Driver settings SetAddress() , GetAddress() , SetTimeoutMs() , GetTimeoutMs() Every call is noexcept and returns DriverResult<T> ( .ok() , .value , .error ) or, for the raw read, a bare DriverError . Check it: a failed call leaves value default-constructed. Talk to several instruments ¶ Driver flow_in ( uart , 1 ); // one Driver per instrument, all on the same port Driver flow_out ( uart , 2 , 100 ); // a 100 ms response timeout for this one flow_out . SetTimeoutMs ( 250 ); // change it later The constructor sends nothing. The port must outlive every driver that uses it. Drivers that share a port must not run at the same time ( Porting ). Identify the instrument ¶ const auto r = meter . ReadIdentity (); // registers 25, 26..31 and 45..49: three requests if ( ! r . ok ()) { return false ; } id = r . value ; const double full_scale = id . full_scale_flow_raw / 1000.0 ; // registers 47-48: value / 1000 std :: printf ( "FW %u.%u.%u SN %s full scale %.3f %s 
 " , id . fw_major , id . fw_minor , id . fw_patch , id . serial_number , full_scale , al :: ToString ( id . flow_units ). data ()); ReadIdentity() costs three requests. Read it once at start-up and keep the result: the flow units and full scale tell you how to interpret every flow value. Read live data ¶ const auto r = meter . ReadInstantaneous ( 3 ); // 3: the instrument's factory-set flow decimals if ( r . ok ()) { const al :: InstantaneousData & d = r . value ; std :: printf ( "%s %.2f C flow %.3f total %.3f setpoint %.3f valve %.1f %% 
 " , al :: GasShortName ( d . gas ). data (), static_cast < double > ( d . temperature_c ), static_cast < double > ( d . flow ), static_cast < double > ( d . total_volume ), static_cast < double > ( d . setpoint ), static_cast < double > ( d . valve_drive_pct )); if ( d . mass_flow_overrange || d . temperature_overrange || d . totalizer_overrange ) { std :: printf ( "over range 
 " ); } } One request reads registers 2100 to 2109. Temperature and valve drive are always value / 100. Flow, total, setpoint and batch are divided by 10 decimals , where decimals (default 3) is the factory-set number of decimal places of the instrument. The manual names no register that reports it: check one reading against the ASCII data frame or the calibration sheet and fix the value in your code. The raw register values are in the raw_* fields for logging. Command a setpoint ¶ // Controllers only. Order: source, watchdog, setpoint. if ( ! controller . SetSetpointSource ( al :: SetpointSource :: DigitalUnsaved ). ok ()) { return false ; // a meter answers ModbusException } if ( ! controller . SetCommWatchdogMs ( 1000 ). ok ()) { // zero setpoint after 1 s without traffic return false ; } return controller . SetSetpoint ( 2.5f ). ok (); // 2.5 in the instrument's flow units Step Why SetSetpointSource(DigitalUnsaved) With Analog the instrument ignores digital setpoints. DigitalSaved stores every setpoint in flash; the manual warns that changing it more often than every few minutes can wear the memory out SetCommWatchdogMs(ms) 0 to 5000 ms. The controller forces a zero setpoint and closes the valve when no serial traffic arrives in time. It works only with DigitalUnsaved SetSetpoint(value) Writes value × 1000 as a signed 32-bit integer to 2053-2054. The instrument rounds to its own resolution ReadInstantaneous().value.setpoint reads back the setpoint in use, which lags the command while a ramp ( SetMaxSetpointRamp() ) is active. Tare and the totalizer ¶ // With the process gas in the line and no flow: if ( const auto r = meter . Tare (); ! r . ok ()) { std :: printf ( "tare: %s 
 " , al :: ToString ( r . error ). data ()); } meter . ResetTotalizer (); // total volume back to 0 meter . SetTotalizerLimitMode ( al :: TotalizerLimitMode :: SaturateWithOvr ); Tare with the process gas in the line and no flow: the manual says BASIS instruments reach their accuracy only when tared on pure process gas. A tare interrupts a running measurement window. The totalizer is lost when power is lost. SetTotalizerBatch() takes the volume already scaled to the total-volume decimals. Measure over a window ¶ controller . ConfigureMeasurementTrigger ( al :: MeasurementTrigger :: OnDigitalSetpointChange ); controller . StartMeasurementSamples ( 400 ); // 400 samples at about 2.5 ms: about 1 s // ... wait at least as long as the window ... const auto m = controller . ReadMeasurement (); if ( m . ok ()) { std :: printf ( "min %d max %d avg %d (raw flow), avg %.2f C 
 " , m . value . min_flow_raw , m . value . max_flow_raw , m . value . avg_flow_raw , static_cast < double > ( m . value . avg_temperature_c )); } The instrument samples about every 2.5 ms. Writing the sample count starts a new window and moves the running one into the "previous" registers. Use the raw minimum, maximum and average flow with the same decimals as live flow. Find and readdress instruments ¶ std :: array < uint8_t , 32 > present {}; // bit N set: an instrument answered at address N const auto r = probe . DiscoverPresentAddresses ( present . data (), present . size ()); if ( r . ok ()) { for ( unsigned a = 1 ; a <= al :: kMaxModbusAddress ; ++ a ) { if ( present [ a / 8 ] & ( 1U << ( a % 8 ))) { std :: printf ( "instrument at %u 
 " , a ); } } } The sweep reads register 25 at each address with a 30 ms timeout (by default): a full sweep of 247 empty addresses takes about 7.5 s. It restores the driver's address and timeout afterwards. It finds instruments at the host's current baud rate only. // Only this instrument on the bus, or only one at the old address. if ( ! meter . SetModbusAddress ( 12 ). ok ()) { return false ; } return meter . GetAddress () == 12 ; // the driver now talks to address 12 Give each instrument a unique address before you connect the next one: two instruments at one address answer on top of each other. Change the baud rate ¶ // The instrument switches as soon as it receives the write, so its reply may be garbled. meter . SetBaudRate ( al :: BaudRate :: Bps_115200 ); set_host_baud ( al :: BaudRateToBps ( al :: BaudRate :: Bps_115200 )); return meter . ReadIdentity (). ok (); // confirm at the new rate The instrument switches before it answers The manual warns that the host must change its own rate in time to receive the confirmation, and may not. Treat the result of SetBaudRate() as unreliable, switch the host UART, then confirm with a read at the new rate. If that fails, sweep the six rates to find the instrument again. Use any register directly ¶ uint16_t full_scale_sccm [ 2 ]{}; // registers 35-36: full scale in SCCM, unsigned 32-bit if ( meter . ReadHoldingRegisters ( al :: reg :: FullScaleFlowSccm , full_scale_sccm , 2 ) == al :: DriverError :: None ) { const uint32_t sccm = ( static_cast < uint32_t > ( full_scale_sccm [ 0 ]) << 16 ) | full_scale_sccm [ 1 ]; std :: printf ( "full scale %lu SCCM 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( sccm )); } meter . WriteSingleRegister ( al :: reg :: TareSampleCount , 400 ); // register 51: samples per tare The register constants are in alicat_basis2::reg ; the Modbus-RTU protocol page lists them with their scaling. ReadHoldingRegisters() reads up to 32 registers; WriteMultipleRegisters() writes up to 32. Handle errors ¶ const auto r = meter . ReadInstantaneous (); if ( ! r . ok ()) { switch ( r . error ) { case al :: DriverError :: Timeout : // no reply: wiring, baud rate, address, timeout case al :: DriverError :: BadCrc : // noise, termination, a second slave answering break ; case al :: DriverError :: ModbusException : // the instrument refused: register, value, meter vs controller break ; default : std :: printf ( "%s 
 " , al :: ToString ( r . error ). data ()); break ; } } DriverError Meaning Where to look Timeout No byte arrived within the timeout Wiring, baud rate, address, DE/RE, the timeout InvalidFrame Too short, wrong byte count; also an exception reply to a write (see below) Line noise, a register a meter does not have BadCrc CRC-16 mismatch Ground, termination, two instruments at one address ModbusException The instrument returned an exception to a read Register not implemented by this model or firmware ResponseMismatch Reply from another address, or an echo that differs from the request Address clash, a late reply from an earlier request InvalidParameter , InvalidAddress The driver refused the argument; nothing was sent Ranges on the Configuration page BufferTooSmall A request longer than the driver's 32-register buffers Split the access Exceptions to writes An exception reply is 5 bytes; the write calls expect an 8-byte reply, so today a rejected write (for example SetSetpointSource() on a meter) returns InvalidFrame after the full timeout, not ModbusException . The status bits in InstantaneousData ( mass_flow_overrange , temperature_overrange , totalizer_overrange , valve_held , valve_thermal_management ) report instrument conditions, not transport errors. Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the instrument. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application holds one Driver object per instrument on the bus; its public calls (listed from inc/alicat_basis2.hpp) turn into holding-register reads and writes. The Modbus-RTU layer (inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp) builds function 03, 06 and 16 frames and checks the CRC-16 of every reply. The platform port is the only code you write: a class derived from UartInterface (inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp) that writes bytes, reads bytes with a timeout and flushes the receive buffer. Below it are the UART, the RS-485 or RS-232 transceiver and the instruments. Drawn from: inc/alicat_basis2.hpp Driver members ; inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp frame builders ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp UartInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it Hardware-agnostic core : Driver<UartT> inc/alicat_basis2.hpp Never, for a new board Modbus-RTU framing : alicat_basis2::modbus inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp Never Platform port : your class Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) The core depends only on the port's methods; the framing depends on nothing. The port derives from UartInterface in inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp and calls your SDK. Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test mock. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the instrument ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as Driver participant M as modbus participant P as Your port A->>D: SetSetpoint(2.5) D->>D: 2.5 x 1000 = 2500, split into two registers D->>M: BuildWriteMultiple(addr, 2053, regs, 2) M-->>D: 13-byte frame with CRC-16 D->>P: flush_rx() D->>P: write(frame) D->>P: read(rx, 8, timeout) P-->>D: 8 reply bytes (or fewer on timeout) D->>M: ParseWriteMultipleEcho(rx, addr, 2053, 2) M-->>D: DriverError::None D-->>A: DriverResult<void> ok Every public call is one or more of these exchanges: flush, write the request, read the expected reply length with the timeout, check it. A broadcast (address 0) write returns as soon as the request is written; no instrument replies to it. Why CRTP ¶ The port is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: Driver<MyUart> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too. Results, not exceptions ¶ Every call returns DriverResult<T> (a value and a DriverError ) or a bare DriverError , and is noexcept . DriverResult converts to bool , so if (auto r = meter.Tare(); !r) works. ToString(DriverError) gives a stable name for logs without allocating. The API guide lists what each error means. One driver per address ¶ A Driver holds a reference to the port, one Modbus address and one timeout: three members, no buffers that outlive a call. Several drivers can share one port, one per instrument on a multidrop bus. The driver does not lock anything; one task must own the bus, or a mutex must guard every call ( Porting ). docs.text: How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the instrument. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application holds one Driver object per instrument on the bus; its public calls (listed from inc/alicat_basis2.hpp) turn into holding-register reads and writes. The Modbus-RTU layer (inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp) builds function 03, 06 and 16 frames and checks the CRC-16 of every reply. The platform port is the only code you write: a class derived from UartInterface (inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp) that writes bytes, reads bytes with a timeout and flushes the receive buffer. Below it are the UART, the RS-485 or RS-232 transceiver and the instruments. docs.text: The port is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: Driver<MyUart> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too.

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a BASIS-2, with which bus settings, and the wiring traps to avoid. All values here come from the BASIS-2 operation manual (Rev 4, May 2025) unless a row says it is derived. The manual covers both B-Series meters and BC-Series controllers; rows marked "controllers" do not apply to meters. Connector ¶ Power and signals share the 6-pin JST-GH connector on top of the instrument. Pin Signal Notes 1 Analog setpoint in, or tare Controllers: setpoint input. Meters: hold to ground for 25 ms or more to tare 2 Analog out 0 V to 5 V or 4 mA to 20 mA, linear in flow 3 Ground Common to power, serial and analog signals 4 Power in 12 V to 24 V DC 5 RS-232 Rx, or RS-485 B (+) The model decides RS-232 or RS-485 6 RS-232 Tx, or RS-485 A (−) Power on pin 4 only Power on any other pin can permanently damage the instrument. Do not connect the analog lines to a loop-powered 4 mA to 20 mA system: the manual says it destroys parts of the circuit; use a signal isolator and a separate supply. Wiring ¶ RS-485 RS-232 From To MCU UART TX Transceiver DI MCU UART RX Transceiver RO MCU GPIO or RTS Transceiver DE and RE, tied Transceiver A BASIS-2 pin 6 (A −) Transceiver B BASIS-2 pin 5 (B +) MCU GND Transceiver GND, BASIS-2 pin 3 Any half-duplex 3.3 V transceiver works (SN65HVD11, MAX3485 and similar). The ESP32 examples use UART1 with TX on GPIO17, RX on GPIO18 and DE/RE on GPIO8 (RTS), with ESP-IDF's UART_MODE_RS485_HALF_DUPLEX driving the direction pin. From To MCU UART TX RS-232 transceiver T1IN; T1OUT to BASIS-2 pin 5 (Rx) MCU UART RX RS-232 transceiver R1OUT; R1IN from BASIS-2 pin 6 (Tx) MCU GND Transceiver GND, BASIS-2 pin 3 RS-232 is point to point: one instrument per UART. Use a level shifter (MAX3232 or similar); never connect pins 5 and 6 to 3.3 V logic directly. Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Frame 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit Baud rate 4800, 9600, 19200, 38400 (default), 57600, 115200 (register 21) Modbus address 1 to 247 (register 45); an out-of-range write sets 1 Function codes 03 read holding, 06 write single, 16 write multiple Byte order Big-endian registers; 32-bit values high register first Response timeout 200 ms, the driver default ( kDefaultTimeoutMs ); the manual gives no figure The manual does not state a factory Modbus address. Find it with DiscoverPresentAddresses() on a bus with one instrument ( API guide ). Timing ¶ Modbus-RTU ends a frame with an idle gap of 3.5 characters, and a new frame must not start sooner. The driver writes a request, then reads the reply; it does not insert a gap itself, so the port or the UART must leave it ( Porting ). Baud Byte (8N1) 3.5-char gap Live-data exchange 9600 1.04 ms 3.65 ms 34.4 ms 19200 0.52 ms 1.82 ms 17.2 ms 38400 0.26 ms 1.75 ms 8.6 ms 115200 0.087 ms 1.75 ms 2.9 ms The live-data exchange is ReadInstantaneous() : an 8-byte request and a 25-byte reply. These figures are derived from the baud rate and the Modbus over Serial Line specification (10 bits per byte at 8N1; a fixed 1.75 ms gap above 19200 baud), not measured. The instrument's own turnaround comes on top; the manual does not specify it. sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant B as BASIS-2 at address 1 H->>B: 01 03 08 34 00 0A CRC (read 2100..2109) Note over B: processes after a 3.5-character idle B-->>H: 01 03 14 (20 data bytes) CRC H->>B: 01 10 08 05 00 02 04 00 07 A1 20 CRC (setpoint 500000 to 2053-2054) B-->>H: 01 10 08 05 00 02 CRC Power ¶ Instrument Supply Current BC-Series controller 12 V to 24 V DC 210 mA B-Series meter 12 V to 24 V DC 12 mA Connect the MCU ground to pin 3. The analog output and the serial lines share that ground; long runs drop voltage on it, so use a heavy ground wire when you also read the analog output. Status LED ¶ LED Meaning Solid green Powered, no errors Flashing green Powered, serial activity Fast red blink Mass flow, temperature or totalizer over range ( MOV , TOV , OVR ) Slow red blink Valve hold or valve thermal management ( HLD , VTM ) Process connections ¶ Model range NPT SAE 100 SCCM to 2 SLPM ⅛" SAE4 5 SLPM to 20 SLPM ⅜" SAE6 Mount the flow body horizontally with the flow arrow parallel to the ground; the maximum common-mode pressure is 145 PSIG. The manual suggests a 50 µm in-line filter and no pipe dope on the ports. RS-485 bus practice ¶ These are general RS-485 rules, not from the Alicat manual: One twisted pair as a trunk, 120 Ω termination at both ends, short stubs to each instrument. Modbus addresses go to 247, but a standard transceiver drives 32 unit loads; check your transceivers' load rating before you put many instruments on one segment. Bias resistors (or a fail-safe transceiver) keep the idle bus in a defined state. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++17 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++17 compiler: GCC 8+, Clang 7+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses if constexpr , std::string_view and std::void_t . CMake 3.16 or newer, for the version header and the target. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call is noexcept and returns DriverResult<T> or DriverError . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-alicat-basis2-driver.git external/hf-alicat-basis2-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-alicat-basis2-driver Only inc/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-alicat-basis2-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::alicat_basis2 ) hf::alicat_basis2 is an alias of the INTERFACE target hf_alicat_basis2 . It carries the include directories ( inc/ and the generated version header) and requires C++17 ( cxx_std_17 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_ALICAT_BASIS2_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF Adds -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic to targets that link the driver HF_ALICAT_BASIS2_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_alicat_basis2/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_ALICAT_BASIS2_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_alicat_basis2 . How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_alicat_basis2_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, package config, host tests ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_alicat_basis2/CMakeLists.txt IDF component wrapper over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into alicat_basis2_version.h (in the build tree, under hf_alicat_basis2_generated/ ) at configure time. Read it at run time: const char * v = alicat_basis2 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0" The same string is the macro HF_ALICAT_BASIS2_VERSION_STRING . Headers ¶ Header Contents alicat_basis2.hpp Driver<UartT> ; include this one, it includes the rest alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp UartInterface<Derived> , the base of your port alicat_basis2_types.hpp DriverError , DriverResult<T> , gases, units, baud rates, decoded data alicat_basis2_registers.hpp Register addresses ( alicat_basis2::reg ) and function codes alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp Frame builders, parsers and the CRC-16 ( alicat_basis2::modbus ) Next ¶ Quickstart wires an instrument and reads flow; Porting writes the serial interface for your MCU.

docs.text: Modbus-RTU protocol ¶ The frames the driver sends, the registers behind each call, and how values are scaled, from the operation manual's register tables. Function codes ¶ The BASIS-2 implements three Modbus functions, and the driver uses all three. Code Name Driver Reply 0x03 Read holding registers ReadHoldingRegisters() , every read call Address, 0x03 , byte count, data, CRC 0x06 Write single register WriteSingleRegister() , every 16-bit write An echo of the request 0x10 Write multiple registers WriteMultipleRegisters() , the 32-bit writes Address, 0x10 , start register, count, CRC A rejected request gets an exception reply: the function code with bit 7 set ( 0x83 , 0x86 , 0x90 ), an exception code and the CRC. The write-single echo carries the value the host sent, not the value the instrument stored: an out-of-range setpoint is adjusted inside the instrument but echoed unchanged. Read the register back when you need the stored value. Reading an undefined register may return 0 or an exception. Frame format ¶ Field Size (bytes) Notes Address 1 1 to 247; 0 is broadcast (writes only, no reply) Function 1 0x03 , 0x06 , 0x10 ; bit 7 set in an exception reply Data 1 to 69 Big-endian register addresses, counts and values CRC-16 2 Polynomial 0xA001 (reflected 0x8005 ), initial value 0xFFFF , low byte first The driver sends the data addresses of the manual's tables unchanged: register 2100 is 0x0834 in the request. The driver reads at most 32 registers and writes at most 32 in one request (its buffer sizes). Instantaneous data (2053 to 2109) ¶ Register Contents Scaling Field 2053-2054 (R/W) Commanded setpoint, signed 32-bit; takes effect when 2054 is written value / 1000 SetSetpoint() 2100 (R/W) Selected gas number Gas gas , SetGas() 2101 (R) Status: +1 MOV , +2 TOV , +4 OVR , +8 HLD , +16 VTM bits *_overrange , valve_held , valve_thermal_management 2102 (R) Temperature, signed value / 100 = °C temperature_c 2103 (R) Flow, signed 16-bit factory-set decimals flow 2104-2105 (R) Total volume since power-up or reset factory-set decimals total_volume 2106 (R) Current setpoint (may lag the command while ramping) setpoint 2107 (R) Valve drive value / 100 = % valve_drive_pct 2108-2109 (R) Batch volume remaining as 2104-2105 batch_remaining ReadInstantaneous(decimals) reads 2100 to 2109 in one request and divides flow, total, setpoint and batch by 10 decimals . The manual says these registers carry a "factory-set number of decimal places" but names no register that reports it; take it from the instrument's calibration sheet or compare with the ASCII data frame. The setpoint write is always value / 1000, whatever the decimals. docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the serial interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls three methods on a class you derive from alicat_basis2::UartInterface<Self> (in inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application holds one Driver object per instrument on the bus; its public calls (listed from inc/alicat_basis2.hpp) turn into holding-register reads and writes. The Modbus-RTU layer (inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp) builds function 03, 06 and 16 frames and checks the CRC-16 of every reply. The platform port is the only code you write: a class derived from UartInterface (inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp) that writes bytes, reads bytes with a timeout and flushes the receive buffer. Below it are the UART, the RS-485 or RS-232 transceiver and the instruments. Drawn from: inc/alicat_basis2.hpp Driver members ; inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp frame builders ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp UartInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract write(const uint8_t* data, std::size_t length) yes Send all length bytes; return once they are accepted by the UART (better: on the wire) read(uint8_t* out, std::size_t max, uint32_t timeout_ms) yes Return when max bytes arrived or timeout_ms passed; the return value is the number of bytes in out flush_rx() yes Discard every byte already received delay_ms_impl(uint32_t ms) optional Sleep; UartInterface::delay_ms() calls it when present and does nothing otherwise The driver calls flush_rx() , then write() , then one read() with the exact reply length it expects, for every request. It does not call delay_ms() today. The port ¶ my_uart.hpp class MyUart : public alicat_basis2 :: UartInterface < MyUart > { public : // Send a whole Modbus request; return once the last byte is on the wire. void write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t length ) noexcept { platform_uart_write ( data , length ); } // Wait for up to `max` bytes; return early only when all of them arrived. std :: size_t read ( uint8_t * out , std :: size_t max , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( out , max , timeout_ms ); } // Drop stale bytes (a late reply, line noise) before the next request. void flush_rx () noexcept { platform_uart_flush_rx (); } // Optional: a real sleep for UartInterface::delay_ms(). void delay_ms_impl ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_ms ( ms ); } }; Rules for the transfer ¶ Wait for the whole reply. The driver asks for the exact length of a good reply (8 bytes for a write, 5 + 2N for a read of N registers). A read() that returns after the first chunk gives the driver a partial frame: InvalidFrame or BadCrc that come and go. Return what you have at the timeout. A Modbus exception reply is 5 bytes, shorter than the driver asked for; returning the partial bytes lets the driver decode the exception. Leave the 3.5-character gap. A new request must start at least 3.5 characters (1.75 ms above 19200 baud) after the previous reply ended ( Hardware ). A read that returns on the last byte followed at once by the next call's write() can break it; wait in write() if your UART does not. Turn the bus around. On RS-485, assert DE/RE for the request and release it right after the last stop bit, or the instrument's reply collides with your driver. Prefer the UART's hardware RS-485 mode (ESP-IDF UART_MODE_RS485_HALF_DUPLEX , STM32 DEM ) over a GPIO toggled in software. 8N1 at the instrument's baud rate. 38400 out of the factory. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples define EspUartAdapter in alicat_basis2_minimal_example.cpp : ESP-IDF uart_write_bytes() , uart_read_bytes() (which returns at max bytes or the timeout), uart_flush_input() and vTaskDelay() , with UART1 in RS-485 half-duplex mode. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it. Call ReadIdentity() : a serial number that matches the label proves the whole path. Call ReadInstantaneous() in a loop for a minute: no BadCrc or InvalidFrame on a healthy link. Call a write the instrument rejects (for example SetCommWatchdogMs() on a meter): it should fail after about one timeout, not hang. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give the bus one owner task, or guard every call on every driver that shares a port with one mutex. Instruments on separate UARTs can run in parallel.

Call ReadIdentity() : a serial number that matches the label proves the whole path. Call ReadInstantaneous() in a loop for a minute: no BadCrc or InvalidFrame on a healthy link. Call a write the instrument rejects (for example SetCommWatchdogMs() on a meter): it should fail after about one timeout, not hang.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Read flow from a BASIS-2 on your MCU: wire the bus and power, write a small port class, call two driver functions. Power goes to pin 4 only The manual warns that power on any pin other than pin 4 can permanently damage the instrument. Wire every signal before you switch on the 12 V to 24 V supply. 1. Wire it ¶ The usual setup is RS-485 through a half-duplex transceiver; the instrument's model decides whether pins 5 and 6 are RS-485 or RS-232. From To Notes MCU UART TX Transceiver DI 8N1, 38400 baud out of the factory MCU UART RX Transceiver RO MCU GPIO or RTS Transceiver DE and RE, tied High while the MCU transmits Transceiver A BASIS-2 pin 6, A (−) 6-pin JST-GH on top Transceiver B BASIS-2 pin 5, B (+) MCU GND Transceiver GND, BASIS-2 pin 3 One common ground 12 V to 24 V DC BASIS-2 pin 4 Last, after everything else The Hardware page has the RS-232 wiring, the bus settings and the power figures. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf::alicat_basis2 CMake target (or put inc/ on the include path and build with C++17). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-alicat-basis2-driver.git external/hf-alicat-basis2-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. It writes bytes, reads bytes with a timeout and flushes the receive buffer. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_uart.hpp class MyUart : public alicat_basis2 :: UartInterface < MyUart > { public : // Send a whole Modbus request; return once the last byte is on the wire. void write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t length ) noexcept { platform_uart_write ( data , length ); } // Wait for up to `max` bytes; return early only when all of them arrived. std :: size_t read ( uint8_t * out , std :: size_t max , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read ( out , max , timeout_ms ); } // Drop stale bytes (a late reply, line noise) before the next request. void flush_rx () noexcept { platform_uart_flush_rx (); } // Optional: a real sleep for UartInterface::delay_ms(). void delay_ms_impl ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_ms ( ms ); } }; read() must wait until max bytes have arrived or the timeout has passed, then return what it has. Porting explains each method and the RS-485 direction pin. 4. Read flow ¶ main.cpp #include "alicat_basis2.hpp" #include <cstdio> int read_flow_once ( MyUart & uart ) { alicat_basis2 :: Driver < MyUart > meter ( uart , 1 ); // Modbus address 1, 200 ms timeout const auto id = meter . ReadIdentity (); // 1. who is on the bus if ( ! id . ok ()) { std :: printf ( "no reply: %s \n " , alicat_basis2 :: ToString ( id . error ). data ()); return -1 ; // wiring, baud rate or address } const auto live = meter . ReadInstantaneous ( 3 ); // 2. one request: registers 2100..2109 if ( ! live . ok ()) { return -1 ; } std :: printf ( "SN %s %s flow %.3f %s %.2f C \n " , id . value . serial_number , alicat_basis2 :: GasShortName ( live . value . gas ). data (), static_cast < double > ( live . value . flow ), alicat_basis2 :: ToString ( id . value . flow_units ). data (), static_cast < double > ( live . value . temperature_c )); return 0 ; } What each step does: Driver<MyUart>(uart, 1) targets Modbus address 1 with the default 200 ms response timeout. Nothing is sent yet. ReadIdentity() reads the firmware version, serial number, address, unit ID, full scale and flow units. A reply proves the wiring, the baud rate and the address. ReadInstantaneous(3) reads registers 2100 to 2109 in one request. The 3 is the number of decimals the instrument's flow registers carry; see API guide . This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check Timeout on every call Baud rate (38400 default), A and B swapped, DE/RE not driven, wrong address BadCrc A missing common ground, termination on a long bus, two instruments at one address flow is 10 or 100 times off The decimals passed to ReadInstantaneous() ( API guide ) The LED blinks red fast Mass flow, temperature or totalizer over range ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : setpoints, taring, the totalizer, errors. Examples : complete ESP32-S3 applications. Modbus-RTU protocol : frames, registers and what each call sends.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host unit tests against a model of the instrument, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. Host unit tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a mock UART that behaves like a BASIS-2 Modbus slave: holding registers in a map, an echo for function 06, address and count for function 16, exception 02 for a register the model does not have, silence for another address, and a switch to corrupt the CRC. cmake -S . -B build-host -DHF_ALICAT_BASIS2_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build-host ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_modbus.cpp CRC-16 against the Modbus specification example, request builders, reply parsing tests/test_driver.cpp Identity, live data scaling, setpoint encoding, magic values, range checks, address change, errors, discovery tests/mock_basis2.hpp The instrument model Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target hf_alicat_basis2_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. CI workflows ¶ Workflow What it checks Host unit tests GCC and Clang build and run the tests and the doc snippets ESP32 examples build Every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type C++ lint, C++ analysis clang-format, clang-tidy and cppcheck Docs Strict site build, figure and generated-table drift, Doxygen, link check, Lighthouse budget Markdown lint, YAML lint, link check Repository text files The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools and hf-espidf-ci-tools . On hardware ¶ The ESP32 examples are the hardware test: alicat_basis2_full_example walks every feature and logs the result of each call over the serial monitor. Run it on a meter and on a controller after any change to the driver.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up a BASIS-2, their causes and the fix for each, cheapest check first. Start with the DriverError of the failing call and the LED: they tell transport problems (no reply, bad CRC) apart from instrument conditions (over range, valve hold). No reply ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Timeout on every call, LED solid green Wrong baud rate The factory rate is 38400 8N1; if someone changed it, sweep 4800 to 115200 Timeout on every call, LED never flashes green Nothing reaches the instrument A and B swapped, DE/RE never asserted, TX and RX swapped, RS-232 model on an RS-485 bus Timeout at one address only Wrong address DiscoverPresentAddresses() with only that instrument on the bus Timeout after SetBaudRate() The host UART is still at the old rate Switch the host rate, then ReadIdentity() ( API guide ) Timeout after FactoryRestore() Bus settings back to the factory values Power-cycle, then rediscover Corrupted replies ¶ Symptom Cause Fix BadCrc or InvalidFrame now and then Noise, no termination on a long bus, no common ground 120 Ω at both ends, ground to pin 3, twisted pair BadCrc every time at one address Two instruments at the same address Disconnect all but one, SetModbusAddress() , repeat InvalidFrame that comes and goes The port's read() returns before all bytes arrived Wait for max bytes or the timeout ( Porting ) ResponseMismatch A late reply to an earlier request Raise the timeout; flush_rx() must drop stale bytes The instrument refuses ¶ Symptom Cause Fix A write returns InvalidFrame after a full timeout An exception reply to the write (a meter has no control registers) Expected on meters; see API guide ModbusException on a read The register is not in this firmware (many were added in V3.0.0) Read the firmware version (register 25) Setpoint writes have no effect Setpoint source is Analog SetSetpointSource(SetpointSource::DigitalUnsaved) Setpoint jumps to 0, valve closes Communication watchdog expired Poll faster than the watchdog, or SetCommWatchdogMs(0) The setpoint read back differs from the command A ramp is active, or the instrument rounded it SetMaxSetpointRamp(0) to disable ramping Readings look wrong ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Flow 10, 100 or 1000 times off Wrong decimals passed to ReadInstantaneous() Compare with the ASCII data frame or calibration sheet ( API guide ) Negative or offset flow at zero Poor tare Tare on the process gas with no flow; controllers: enable autotare Readings inaccurate after a gas change Old gas still in the line, or not tared on the new gas Flow the new gas long enough, then tare Readings will not settle The instrument is fast and sees real fluctuation SetFlowAveragingMs() ; tune P and I (registers 519, 520) Controller does not reach its setpoint Supply pressure too low, or a blocked port Raise inlet pressure; check for thread tape in the ports LED blinks red fast, mass_flow_overrange set Flow above the range Reduce flow; check the full scale with ReadIdentity() LED blinks red slowly, valve_thermal_management set A setpoint with no flow for a while Check that gas is supplied; the valve resumes when flow changes Getting help ¶ Open an issue at https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-alicat-basis2-driver/issues with the driver version ( GetDriverVersion() ), the output of ReadIdentity() , your platform and a byte trace of the failing request and reply.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Three layers, one of them yours ¶ Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application holds one Driver object per instrument on the bus; its public calls (listed from inc/alicat_basis2.hpp) turn into holding-register reads and writes. The Modbus-RTU layer (inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp) builds function 03, 06 and 16 frames and checks the CRC-16 of every reply. The platform port is the only code you write: a class derived from UartInterface (inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp) that writes bytes, reads bytes with a timeout and flushes the receive buffer. Below it are the UART, the RS-485 or RS-232 transceiver and the instruments.
